subject: Spend band spot-check + PO handoff (next steps)
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Sondra Patel <sondra@fintechcorp.com>, Mike Lowe <mike.lowe@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Spend band spot-check + PO handoff (next steps)

Hi Sondra / Mike —

Thanks again for a productive 30-min call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we loop procurement: 

Recap
- Primary use: customer support summarization + triage (median input length ~400 tokens).
- Expected volume: bursty, starting small in month 1 and ramping to steady usage. You called out a likely steady-state spend range rather than raw token volumes.

Cost & budget follow-up (two asks)
1) Confirm the monthly spend band you expect (helps us decide commitment tier). You mentioned a target corridor during the call — can you confirm a low/high range (e.g., $Xk–$Yk / month)?
2) Procurement threshold for requiring a formal PO (and any internal approval owners we should loop). You mentioned legal review kicks in at a spend level — please confirm that dollar threshold.

To make the economics concrete: for reference, our hosted public list baseline for text generation is $1,200 per 1M tokens. Typical commitment discounts and negotiated reserved pricing can bring that down (examples attached). See pricing_sheet_v3.xlsx [Attachment: pricing_sheet_v3.xlsx (XLSX, 72KB)].

Proposed next steps
- Sondra / Mike: confirm monthly spend band and procurement PO threshold.
- Diego: share a short one-page pricing summary and suggested PO wording once band is confirmed.
- Karthik / Monica: prepare a one-way DocuSign for the PO and SOC2 summary if procurement asks for it.

If it helps, we can also map the spend band to an equivalent token burn at the model/usage profile you described — I can send a short table once you confirm the $ band.

Thanks — looking to get procurement moving this week.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: pricing_sheet_v3.xlsx]

From: Sondra Patel <sondra@fintechcorp.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Mike Lowe <mike.lowe@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Spend band spot-check + PO handoff (next steps)

Diego —

Appreciate the recap. Short answers below so we can escalate to procurement: 

- Monthly spend band: our current internal planning range is $8k–$18k / month for the pilot -> early production window. That maps roughly to the mid-tier traffic you saw on the demo.
- Procurement PO threshold: a formal PO > $10,000 requires legal review and our procurement lead (Lynn). Anything <= $10k can be processed by our platform ops team.
- Discount ask: if we commit to 6 months at the higher end of the band (>= $15k/mo), we would expect a unit target closer to $800–$900 per 1M tokens. Is that in scope?

We also need a short SOC2 summary for our security intake — ideally a one-page that lists scope and last audit quarter. Can you attach that?

Next steps for us: I will introduce Lynn (procurement) on the PO thread once we have your confirmed price / PO wording.

Thanks,
Sondra Patel
Head of Integrations, FinTechCorp
sondra@fintechcorp.com

Subject: Re: Spend band spot-check + PO handoff (next steps)

Thanks Sondra — quick clarifications from our side.

1) Pricing math (public hosted baseline vs commit):
- Hosted public list (no commit): $1,200 / 1M tokens.
- 6-month commitment band (predictable monthly commit at or above $15k): negotiable, typical target price we can discuss is $900 / 1M tokens.
- Longer reserved capacity (dedicated GPUs) can push unit economics lower but has a footprint/time commitment.

2) PO flow and timing:
- If procurement threshold is $10k, we can provide PO wording that keeps the first month below that amount (pilot invoice) and then a second PO for committed months if needed.
- Alternatively, procurement can sign a 6-mo commitment with an attached schedule (DocuSign) — we will produce a single-page statement of work + PO template.

3) SOC2 & security docs:
- Attaching a SOC2 summary and the standard security intake sheet. If your security team needs the full report, we can arrange a secure sharing workflow; otherwise the summary typically passes intake.

I've attached the pricing sheet Diego referenced and the SOC2 one-pager.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
[Attachments: pricing_sheet_v3.xlsx, SOC2_Summary.pdf]

From: Sondra Patel <sondra@fintechcorp.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike Lowe <mike.lowe@fintechcorp.com>, Lynn Chao <lynn.chao@fintechcorp.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T13:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Spend band spot-check + PO handoff (next steps)

Karthik / Diego —

Received the attachments, thanks. Quick confirmation:

- We will treat the band as $8k–$18k/mo for internal planning. Procurement will require a PO for anything > $10k — Lynn (cc'd) will manage that.
- We are comfortable starting the pilot with month-to-month invoices while procurement confirms a 6-mo commit option. If you can draft the DocuSign and include the 6-mo committed price schedule (showing the $900 / 1M token line) that will speed approval.
- Security ask: include a data retention statement in the SOW (how long Redwood retains logs/KV cache for hosted workloads) — procurement needs that clause visible.

Lynn — Diego/Karthik will send a one-page PO + SOW that includes the retention language and a DocuSign link. Can you confirm the internal billing contact and whether a single PO can cover multiple pilot environments?

Will follow up once Lynn confirms.

Best,
Sondra Patel
Head of Integrations, FinTechCorp
[External to Redwood: procurement questions — please route to Lynn]
